title: EU ingress/egress policy mediator with allow/deny lattice
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Customers operating under EU data residency requirements need deterministic routing for both ingress and egress such that requests from EU tenants never leave EU regions, while still permitting approved exceptions for specific customer allowlists. Current routing logic mixes region-selection rules with cost/tier routing and lacks a clear precedence model when allow/deny constraints conflict with lower-level fallback strategies.

Goal: Implement a policy mediator component that evaluates a compact allow/deny lattice for each request (tenant-level, org-level, account-level policies) to decide ingress and egress paths. The mediator should: (1) expose deterministic precedence and short-circuiting semantics, (2) integrate with tier routing (hosted vs. dedicated) and model-variant fallbacks, (3) produce audit-ready decisions for compliance, and (4) allow emergency administrative bypass with strong audit and TTL.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change kernel selection, batching heuristics, or cost tiers. It focuses solely on policy evaluation and decision surfaces for routing and fallback selection.
acceptance_criteria: Policy mediator library implemented and exported as internal service with stable v1 API (evaluatePolicy(requestMeta) -> decisionId)
Decision precedence: tenant allowlist > tenant denylist > org allowlist > org denylist > global default; documented and tested
If EU-only residency flag set, decision must pick EU region endpoints or mark as "BLOCKED" and trigger customer notification flow for exceptions
Fallback mapping defined: for each primary model variant, a deterministic, allowed fallback list is provided and validated against policy (no non-EU fallback for EU-only tenants)
End-to-end integration tests cover: allowed exception path, blocked path, tier fallback path, and emergency admin bypass with TTL
Telemetry: each decision emits trace id, matched ruleset keys, final region, chosen capacity tier, chosen model variant, and a compliance_reason string
Migration plan: feature flag gated rollout with canary (1% tenants), metrics dashboard, rollback on >1% requests failing SLO or >0.5% policy mis-evaluations
Conformance: documentation added to Confluence and console UI surfaces for tenant admins to view decision logs (read-only)
updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed. Implemented prototype of lattice evaluator in go-policy module. Key insight: represent allow/deny precedence as weighted tags to enable O(1) evaluation per request. Prototype repo: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/EU+Policy+Lattice+Spike
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and Security. Agreed to require signed admin bypass tokens and 1h TTL. Security requested an audit-event schema; assigned to @Lina Kovacs for event schema PR.

2026-03-06: Decided on deterministic fallback mapping approach: blacklist-based fallbacks (explicit allowlists), not capability inference. Trade-off: slightly more operator overhead but provably compliant.
2026-03-09: Began implementation of decision telemetry. Prototype emits a compact decisionId that can be referenced in console. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8432

2026-03-11: Integration note: mediator will expose GRPC and HTTP endpoints; runtime will cache decision results keyed by (tenantId, primaryModel, regionHint) with TTL=30s to avoid hot-path policy DB hits

2026-03-13: QA tests added for EU-only tenants. Found edge case where dedicated-pool routing attempted non-EU fallback when capacity exhausted. New guard rule added to block any non-EU fallback unless explicit exception exists. Updating canary plan to include stress tests against Dedicated capacity exhaustion scenarios.
